# Introduction

DatasetDNA is a compact package for quickly assessing the quality and readiness of a dataset for machine learning. It summarizes key dimensions of a dataset through a set of score-based "gene" metrics.

# Quick start

```{r setup}
library(DatasetDNA)
```

```{r}
example_path <- system.file("extdata", "example_dataset.csv", package = "DatasetDNA")
example_df <- read.csv(example_path)

example_df
```

# Full dataset analysis

```{r}
report <- dataset_dna(example_df, target = "churn")
print(report)
```

# Interpreting the output

The package returns a structured report that includes:

- dataset summary
- quality score
- completeness score
- complexity score
- balance score
- correlation score
- overall DNA score
- health status
- recommended model type

These metrics are designed to help with early exploratory analysis and machine-learning readiness checks.

# Practical notes

- Use a target column when you want class balance to be measured explicitly.
- The package is best used for fast exploratory and comparative checks rather than formal model evaluation.
- If a dataset has insufficient numeric columns, the correlation score falls back to a safe default rather than stopping the workflow.
